summaryText:
On Vision Sunday, part of the Build My Church series, Pastor Travis Hearn invited the congregation to give thanks for what God has already done and to look ahead to what God is about to do. Using Joshua 3:5, he described Israel standing between past miracles and a promised future, called to consecrate themselves because the Lord would do wonders among them. He paired this with Habakkuk 2:2, encouraging the church to write the vision and make it plain so that everyone can run with it, whether in the church, a marriage, a family, or a business.

Pastor Travis summarized the heart of Impact Church through two passages from Jesus: the Great Commandment (love God with all your heart, soul, and mind, and love your neighbor as yourself) and the Great Commission (go and make disciples of all nations). He stressed that the church aims to make disciples rather than spectators or consumers. He noted that belief alone is not the goal, and that the first Christians were called Christians because their lives looked like Christ. He explained baptism as a picture of dying to self and rising new in Christ, and he reminded listeners to love every neighbor regardless of background or differences.

To show why remembering matters, he pointed to the memorial stones taken from the Jordan and to David recalling past deliverance before facing Goliath. He then shared the story of Impact Church, beginning with his own sense of feeling unqualified when he and his wife Natalie said yes to pastoring in 2010. He described a church that began with very limited resources, a fundraising effort that fell short but was multiplied through unexpected provision, a bank that showed surprising mercy during a financial crisis, rapid growth, and a grand opening in December 2020 after raising funds during a global shutdown. Throughout, he repeated the refrain "Look what the Lord has done" and held on to walking by faith, not by sight.

Looking forward, he outlined next steps. South Scottsdale will have its grand opening on November 1 with live preaching at both campuses. Service times will be 9:00 and 11:00 a.m. in North Scottsdale and 10:00 a.m. in South Scottsdale. He asked for a core group of 100 people to make South Scottsdale their home church through Resurrection Sunday, and he announced the launch of Impact Español with an interest meeting on November 1. He also shared an encouraging prophetic word he received from a fellow pastor about open doors, and he led the church in a declaration that they are builders, not spectators or consumers.

The message closed with an invitation to ask God, "What part are you asking me to play?" and to serve, pray, give, and invite others as everyone helps build God's church.
mainPoints: God is not finished: remembering what He has done builds faith for what He is about to do, so we prepare ourselves and walk by faith, not by sight.
Impact Church's vision rests on the Great Commandment and the Great Commission: loving God and neighbor, and making disciples rather than spectators or consumers.

Every person has a part in building God's church through prayer, serving, giving, and inviting others, as the church takes its next steps with a second campus, live preaching at both locations, and Impact Español.

Monday.scripture: Joshua 3:5 (NIV): "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do amazing things among you."
Monday.focus: Preparing your heart for what God is about to do.
Monday.action: Spend ten quiet minutes setting yourself apart for God. Turn off distractions, thank Him for one thing He has already done, and name one thing you are trusting Him for.
Monday.prayer: Lord, thank you for all you have done in my life. Prepare my heart for what you are about to do, and help me set myself apart for you today. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Habakkuk 2:2 (NIV): "Write down the revelation and make it plain on tablets so that a herald may run with it."
Tuesday.focus: Writing down and clarifying the vision God has given you.
Tuesday.action: Write one or two clear sentences about what you sense God is asking of you in your family, work, or church life. Share it with one trusted person.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, give me clarity about the vision you have for my life, my home, and my church. Help me write it plainly and walk it out faithfully. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Matthew 22:37-39 (NIV): "Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind... Love your neighbor as yourself."
Wednesday.focus: Living the Great Commandment by loving God and neighbor.
Wednesday.action: Send an encouraging message or do a kind act for a neighbor, coworker, or family member, especially someone who sees things differently than you do.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, help me love you with all my heart, soul, and mind. Show me how to love the people around me the way you love them. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Matthew 28:19 (NIV): "Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit."
Thursday.focus: Becoming a disciple who helps make disciples.
Thursday.action: Invite one person to church, a small group, or a midweek service, or encourage a friend with something you are learning from Scripture.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, make me a true disciple, not just a spectator. Give me courage and kindness to invite others to follow you. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Joshua 4:7 (NIV): "These stones are to be a memorial to the people of Israel forever."
Friday.focus: Remembering God's faithfulness to build faith for the future.
Friday.action: Write down three answered prayers or ways God has been faithful to you. Keep the list where you will see it, and thank God for each one.
Friday.prayer: God, I never want to forget what you have done. Let these reminders strengthen my faith for everything still ahead. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 5:7 (NIV): "For we live by faith, not by sight."
Saturday.focus: Taking your place in building God's church with faith.
Saturday.action: Choose one way to help build the church this week: sign up to serve, pray for your pastors and ministries, plan your giving, or invite someone for Sunday.
Saturday.prayer: Father, I want to be a builder in your church. Use my hands, my heart, my time, and my resources, and help me walk by faith even when I cannot see the whole picture. Amen.
